EVA'S WORLD — install and use
=============================

The 27B ("Eva", the agent's model on the Mac) lives in a Minecraft world as a
research toy for autonomous behaviour. Nobody gives her tasks. She wakes up
every few minutes, reads what happened, and decides what to do through a body
that a small model on nova (the body model) drives move by move.

Everything this needs lives in this directory. Eva's mind calls the raw
llama-server directly, so world activity never reaches the agent's memory,
ledgers, verifier or failure census. The one change in the agent itself is
POST /api/slot/outside-call (§4RQ): Eva asks it before each look (refused
while you are active or your conversation is kept) and tells it when she is
done, so the agent restores its saved head instead of re-reading it.
Each look also shows in the agent's own log as a background line, titled
"eva's world" (🧱): why she woke, how long the look took and what she did.


1. HOW IT FITS TOGETHER
-----------------------

  Mac (eva)                                   nova (16 GB, Tailscale 100.83.184.117)
  ---------                                   ---------------------------------------
  llama-server :8088  (the 27B, 1 slot)       llama-server :8088 (body model, 4 slots)
        ^                                            ^
        |  rare: one "look" every 2–60 min           |  every move (~3–9 s each)
        |                                            |
  eva_mind.py  (launchd: com.local.eva-world-mind)   Mindcraft bot "Eva" (node, mineflayer)
        |                                            |        |
        |  HTTP + key                                |        v
        +-----------> hub :8090  <-------------------+   Paper 1.21.6 server :25565
                      (launchd: com.local.eva-world-hub)   (offline mode, RCON :25575)
                      - starts/pauses/stops the world
                      - records every event (append-only, per session)
                      - serves the monitor page + proxies the 3D viewer
                      - API Eva's mind uses (poll / context / decision)

  One look:
    1. eva_mind polls the hub every 20 s. The hub says "due" when the time Eva
       chose has come, or earlier when something needs her: the body died,
       gave up, got stuck, repeats itself, had 6 commands in a row fail
       (once per run of failures), dropped out, or a player spoke. "Stuck" =
       busy (thinking/acting) 5 min without moving 2 blocks; the clock
       restarts after 60 s straight of not being busy (10-26: it ran on
       through an idle stand and fired 41 s into the next goal), not on a
       moment of chat.
    2. eva_mind checks the agent is idle (/api/health foreground_requests == 0,
       no kept conversation, the llama slot free), then asks the agent's
       /api/slot/outside-call "start". Busy or refused: it waits 60 s.
    3. It fetches the diary (what happened since her last look + her journal),
       asks the 27B (thinking on, server default effort), streams the answer.
       The journal she is shown starts at an entry heading and moves only in
       3000-char steps (4500-7500 chars; the whole file stays on disk), so
       consecutive looks share it and llama reuses that part of the prompt
       (10-26: a last-6000-chars window changed it every look; ~500 of
       ~3,500 tokens were reused).
       If you send the agent a request meanwhile, the call is cut off at once
       (llama cancels it) and retried later. Measured: cut off 2 s after a
       request arrived; that request answered normally.
    4. Her decision (a JSON object at the end of her reply) goes back to the
       hub, which applies it: goal / stop / message to the body / something
       said aloud in world chat / a journal entry / when to look again.

  Her freedom: anything a player can do through Mindcraft's commands, chosen
  by her alone. Limits: no code execution (!newAction off), no outbound fetch
  (!searchWiki off), no network beyond the box, no agent tools, and the world
  only runs when you start it.


2. INSTALL (first time)
-----------------------

Prerequisites
  - nova: macOS, Homebrew, the body model's llama-server on :8088 (already there),
    passwordless ssh from the Mac and passwordless sudo on nova.
  - Mac: the agent running, ~/Data/AI/.ghost_api_key present.
  - Read Mojang's EULA: https://aka.ms/MinecraftEULA (the server needs it).

From the Mac, in this directory:

    ACCEPT_MINECRAFT_EULA=yes ./deploy.sh --install

What it does (all re-runnable):
  on nova  (nova/scripts/install_nova.sh)
    - brew: openjdk@21, node@20 (Mindcraft breaks on Node 24+), git
    - Mindcraft cloned to ~/Data/AI/World/mindcraft at pinned commit f6a9556,
      mineflayer pinned to 4.33.0 (Mindcraft's patches need exactly that)
    - Paper 1.21.6 build 48, checked by SHA-256 (on its first start Paper
      itself downloads the vanilla server jar from Mojang once, into
      server/cache/: no account, no login — the only outbound fetch at runtime)
    - server.properties from config/server.properties.template, created once
      (offline mode, Tailscale address only, peaceful, RCON with a random
      password); a re-run refreshes only the bind address and RCON password,
      so a difficulty you set from the monitor stays
    - hub key ~/Data/AI/World/.hub_key (random, chmod 600)
    - apply_patches.sh (see section 6), hub deps from package-lock.json (npm ci)
    - launchd service com.local.eva-world-hub (always on, does NOT start
      the world by itself)
  on the Mac
    - deploy.sh copies the hub key to ~/Data/AI/.world_hub_key
    - mac/install_mac.sh (run as yourself, not with sudo): launchd service com.local.eva-world-mind (always on; calls the 27B
      only while the world runs and the agent is idle)

Layout on nova after install:
    ~/Data/AI/World/app/        this directory's nova/ (deployed copy)
    ~/Data/AI/World/mindcraft/  Mindcraft
    ~/Data/AI/World/server/     Paper + the world "evaworld"
    ~/Data/AI/World/data/       the research record (see section 5)
    ~/Data/AI/World/run/        logs, pidfiles, hub state


3. USE
------

Monitor (from any device on the tailnet):

    http://100.83.184.117:8090/

  Key: the contents of ~/Data/AI/.world_hub_key (Mac) or
  ~/Data/AI/World/.hub_key (nova). The browser remembers it for 30 days.

  Buttons
    Start   probes the body model, starts the server, starts the bot, waits for it to
            join (~30–60 s). Eva takes her first look right after.
    Pause   freezes game time (/tick freeze) and stops the bot; Eva does not
            look while paused.
    Resume  the reverse.
    Stop    saves and stops everything. The world, the body's memory and
            Eva's journal stay. The next Start opens a NEW session in the
            record (sessions/<date_time>/) in the same world; Eva's first
            look of a session sees only that session's events (plus her
            journal).

  Layout (fits one screen, desktop or phone; only the text scrolls)
    World    3D view (drag to orbit, scroll/pinch to zoom). "Find Eva" puts
             the camera 12 blocks from her, from above, keeping your angle.
    One text panel; the dropdown picks:
      Mind (eva)   each look: why she woke, what she said, what she did;
                   fold-outs with her full reasoning and the diary she saw
      Body (Nova)  every command the small model issued and its result
      Journal      her own notebook, one entry per look
             Newest on top; the newest entry is teal (with a "latest" tag).
             The page remembers your pick.
    History  every past session, replayable

  The page has no talk-to-Eva box on purpose: every human nudge would
  contaminate the record. If you add one later, record it as an
  "intervention" event (the diary already knows how to show that kind).

From the Mac (eva), e.g. over ssh — the eva-world command:

    eva-world status            world phase, where Eva is, what she does, next look
    eva-world start | stop | pause | resume
    eva-world journal           her journal
    eva-world reset             stop + delete EVERYTHING: world, sessions, journal,
                                prompts, body memory. No backup. Asks you to type
                                "yes" (or: reset --yes). The next start makes a
                                new world from a new seed; settings stay.

  It lives in mac/eva-world, linked to ~/.local/bin/eva-world by install_mac.sh.
  A one-off `ssh eva '…'` may not have ~/.local/bin on PATH:
      ssh eva '~/.local/bin/eva-world status'

Without the page (curl):

    K=$(cat ~/Data/AI/.world_hub_key); H=http://100.83.184.117:8090
    curl -s -H "x-world-key: $K" -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' \
         -d '{"action":"start"}' $H/api/control          # start|pause|resume|stop
    curl -s -X POST -H "X-World-Key: $K" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
         -d '{"action":"difficulty","level":"peaceful"}' $H/api/control
                                       # peaceful|easy|normal|hard; live + kept in
                                       # server.properties; recorded as an operator change.
                                       # Default is peaceful: the body's 4-8 s per move is too
                                       # slow to fight. Update mac/world_prompt.txt to match.
    curl -s -X POST -H "X-World-Key: $K" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
         -d '{"action":"note","text":"fixed ..."}' $H/api/control
                                       # record an operator change to the harness;
                                       # Eva's diary shows "the operator intervened: ..."
    curl -s -H "x-world-key: $K" $H/api/status | python3 -m json.tool
    curl -s -H "x-world-key: $K" $H/api/journal

Joining the world yourself (optional): a Minecraft Java 1.21.6 client, any
name, server 100.83.184.117. Offline mode means no account check, which is why
the server listens on the Tailscale address only. Note that joining and
speaking wakes Eva ("<you> spoke in the world"): that is an intervention.
Anyone on the tailnet can join the same way, under any name — joining as
"Eva" kicks the body out (duplicate login). There is no whitelist because
the tailnet is the boundary; add one (whitelist on + whitelist add Eva) if
other people share it.


4. COST TO THE AGENT
--------------------

  - Eva's looks use the 27B's only slot for ~40–65 s each (measured: prefill
    of her ~3–4k-token prompt plus thinking), only while the agent is idle,
    and are cut off the moment you send a request.
  - The agent's 28k head is parked/restored from disk after her call
    (GHOST_HEAD_SAVES=1, ~0.4 s), so no 166 s re-warm.
  - nova: the body model does every move; the agent's own checking work on nova shares
    its 4 slots. Memory with the world running: see section 7.
    Without a pause the body kept nova's GPU at 100% (10-26: the model busy 37 of
    40 s, ~9.5 s per call back to back), slowing that checking work. So the
    body's profile sets "cooldown": 30000 (eva_body.json): its calls to the body model
    START at least 30 s apart (Mindcraft waits before every call: moves, chat,
    memory). Fights and fleeing are code, not calls, so they stay instant;
    Mind's messages wait at most 30 s. Lower it to speed her up.


5. THE RESEARCH RECORD
----------------------

  ~/Data/AI/World/data/sessions/<id>/events.jsonl   one JSON event per line,
      append-only. Kinds: eva_decision (diary, reasoning, reply, parsed
      decision, applied actions, timings, prompt hash), directive,
      body_response, command_result, bot_output, chat, join, leave, death,
      goal_dropped, body_lost/body_restart/body_back, body_process_exit (Mindcraft
      restarted the body itself: an exit code, e.g. its unstuck mode, or a signal), snapshot (every 30 s:
      position, health, hunger, inventory), control, paused/resumed, error,
      mind_status (skipped/interrupted looks).
  ~/Data/AI/World/data/eva/journal.md               her journal
  ~/Data/AI/World/data/eva/prompts/<hash>.txt       every system prompt she
      was given, by hash (each eva_decision names its hash), so a change in
      behaviour can be traced to a change in wording.
  ~/Data/AI/World/mindcraft/bots/Eva/memory.json    the body's own memory


6. CHANGING THINGS
------------------

Edit files HERE, then ./deploy.sh (copies, reinstalls hub deps, restarts the
hub — a running world is adopted, not stopped — and restarts Eva's mind;
that last step needs passwordless sudo on the Mac, otherwise deploy.sh prints
the command to run).

  mac/persona.txt          who Eva is (adapted from the agent's identity text)
  mac/world_prompt.txt     the world framing + decision format. Keep it
                           neutral: it IS the experimental condition.
  nova/config/eva_body.json        the body's model + its prompt
  nova/config/mindcraft_settings.js Mindcraft settings (copied in on start)
  nova/config/server.properties.template  server settings (install only)
  nova/hub/                hub + monitor page

  apply_patches.sh runs before every world start and fails loudly if a patch
  stopped applying:
    - our settings/profile/keys copied over Mindcraft's
    - the 3D viewer listens on 127.0.0.1 only and serves under /viewer
      (reachable only through the hub, behind the key)
    - mineflayer physics guard (scripts/patch_physics.cjs): never send a
      non-finite position. The first session's body was kicked twice for
      "Invalid move player packet received" at the water's edge; with the
      guard it fired once and the body stayed.
    - Paper bStats metrics off
    - the 3D viewer gets a re-centre hook for "Find Eva"
      (scripts/patch_viewer.cjs, into the viewer's minified bundle)
    - Mindcraft's craftRecipe reports a craft only once the server has
      confirmed it (scripts/patch_craft.cjs): it waits 3 s, checks the item
      really arrived, retries once, and otherwise says "did not go through".
      10-26: three wooden pickaxes "crafted" at a table that the server never
      made. Since v2 (10-26 13:09) it crafts ONE item per call and checks
      each (4 torches take ~12 s): mineflayer's own multi-craft clicked from
      a stale inventory ("missing ingredient" after the first of 4 torches).
      If only some land: "Crafted X k of n times; the server undid the rest"
      (or "then: <error>"), worded so the hub does not count it as a failed
      command. v3: a stop request (!stop, a new command, a mode) ends it
      within 0.25 s — Mindcraft kills the body process when an action
      ignores a stop for 10 s, and n crafts take n × 3 s. Each rollback logs "[eva-world] the server rolled back crafting …"
      in run/mindcraft.log.
    - the 3D viewer draws the body with the Noor skin (wide-arm copy) instead
      of Steve: Noor is what a real 1.21 client already shows for an offline
      player named "Eva" (the default skin follows the name's UUID)

  Environment overrides for eva_mind.py (set in the launchd plist):
    EVA_WORLD_HUB, EVA_WORLD_LLAMA, EVA_WORLD_AGENT, EVA_WORLD_POLL_S,
    EVA_WORLD_MAX_TOKENS (default 6000, reasoning + reply)

Tests
    node --test nova/hub/test/*.test.js     (hub, 40 tests)
    pytest tests/test_ai_minecraft.py       (from the agent root: Eva's mind,
                                             config pins, and the hub tests)


7. TROUBLESHOOTING
------------------

Logs
    Mac:  ~/Data/AI/Logs/eva_world_mind.log
    nova: ~/Data/AI/World/run/{hub,server,mindcraft}.log

  "timed out waiting for the body to join" — read run/mindcraft.log. The
      hub stops everything cleanly after a failed start; fix and press Start.
  Body keeps dropping out — the hub restarts it (30 s, 1, 3, 10 min backoff;
      the whole Mindcraft process after 3 tries) and records each attempt.
      grep "lost connection" run/server.log for the server's reason.
  Body ignores every new goal — a running action blocks Mindcraft's goal
      loop (10-26: the body ran !stay(-1), "stay forever", and five goals went
      unanswered). Fixed: the hub sends !stop before each new goal. If it
      comes back, read run/mindcraft.log for "Self-prompt loop is already
      active" with no command after it.
  Eva never looks — monitor's "Eva's mind" tile: "offline" = the Mac service
      is not polling (sudo launchctl kickstart -k system/com.local.eva-world-mind);
      "skipped: agent busy" = the agent is working, she waits.
  Her look ends "no decision JSON found" — recorded as is; she looks again
      in 10 min. If it says it hit the token limit, raise EVA_WORLD_MAX_TOKENS.
  nova memory — the body model's llama-server keeps a host-RAM prompt cache that
      Mindcraft fills (many distinct prompts); it plateaus at its cap
      ("making room for prompt cache entry" in the llama log). Measured with
      the world running: ~23% free, 0.9 GB swap, no Metal OOM. To free ~3 GB,
      add `--cache-ram 2048` to nova's com.local.llama-server.plist.

Start over (new world, empty journal, no body memory)
    eva-world reset (Mac). It stops the world, then nova/scripts/reset_world.sh
    deletes server/evaworld{,_nether,_the_end}, data/sessions/, data/eva/ and
    mindcraft/bots/Eva/ — no backup — and restarts the hub. It refuses while
    the world or any of its processes still runs. Done by hand once on
    2026-10-26 07:32.

Uninstall
    nova: press Stop first (the server and the body run detached and would
          keep running), then
          sudo launchctl bootout system/com.local.eva-world-hub
          sudo rm /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.local.eva-world-hub.plist
          rm -rf ~/Data/AI/World           (deletes the world AND the record)
    Mac:  sudo launchctl bootout system/com.local.eva-world-mind
          sudo rm /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.local.eva-world-mind.plist
          rm ~/Data/AI/.world_hub_key ~/.local/bin/eva-world
